name: Dongjae Kang
bio: is an MPA candidate in Technology Policy and Innovation at Columbia University, with a B.S. in Industrial and Systems Engineering from KAIST. As an intern at the UN Statistics Division, he leads development of a companion to UN Statistical Commission session reports that links each decision to the discussion behind it. He co-first-authored CrisisNews, a 93,250-article dataset presented at News Futures (CHI 2025), and builds PRISM, a news platform publishing daily public-affairs briefs with source provenance across US and Korean media.

name: Sze Wing (Hesper) Lui
bio: is an MPA candidate in Technology Policy and Innovation with a minor in Cybersecurity at Columbia University and an Institute of Global Politics Student Scholar. She previously worked at Hong Kong's Legislative Council and in ESG and climate communications at MSCI. Her current research examines legitimacy laundering and human rights risks in cyberspace.

name: Xuefei (Sophie) Ren
bio: is an MPA candidate in Technology Policy and Innovation at Columbia University. She previously worked on global Smart TV advertising projects at Samsung Ads' PMO team, following management consulting experience at EY. As a McGill Integrated Management Student Fellow, she interviewed researchers at OpenAI and Mila. She has also advised a companion robotics company on product strategy and co-founded an initiative focused on responsible AI and data transparency.

name: Zifu (Tyler) Qin
bio: is a Ph.D. researcher in Systems Engineering at Cornell University. His research spans multimedia forensics, computer vision, signal processing, and trustworthy AI, with interests in robust video analysis, deepfake detection and localization, and media authenticity. His work investigates computational and forensic methods for detecting and localizing manipulated visual content under real-world media transformations. He has also participated in NSF I-Corps, exploring pathways for translating media authentication technologies into practical applications.

name: Sara Shibata
bio: studies International Security and Diplomacy, with a minor in Technology Policy, at Columbia University, where she is Communications Director of SIPA Cyber's Digital and Cyber Program. She has worked at Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and holds a Master of Public Policy from the University of Tokyo, where she researched Japanese youth's civic participation on social media.

name: Crystal Yang
bio: is an MIA candidate at Columbia University, concentrating in Technology Policy and Innovation. Her background spans law, governance, and tax compliance in Australia and the United States. At Wikimedia NYC, she led public programs advancing free knowledge on the internet, and before that held legal and compliance roles at the Australian Taxation Office. She holds a Combined Bachelor Degree in Law and Arts from the University of Sydney, and is admitted as a solicitor in Australia. Crystal's interests include digital safety, digital transformation, AI governance, and information integrity.

name: Sneha Shree Saikia
bio: is an MIA candidate in International Security and Diplomacy with a minor in Tech Policy at Columbia University. Before SIPA, she worked with members of parliament in India on legislation, including a bill on AI regulation, and as an intern in UNDP's Crisis Bureau she worked on information management systems and AI tools for practitioners and country offices.

name: Puyu (Irene) Cui
bio: is a master's student in Computer and Information Science at the University of Pennsylvania, with a background in computer science, statistics, and finance. She works on AI and machine learning, including natural language processing, reinforcement learning, and AI agents.

name: Fio Wibawa
bio: is a dual-degree candidate in the University of Tokyo's Master of Public Policy International Program and Columbia University's Master of International Affairs. At Tokyo, Wibawa follows the Public Management and International Relations stream on law, policy, and emerging technologies, and at Columbia concentrated in Technology Policy and Innovation with a focus on AI governance.
affiliation: The University of Tokyo · Columbia University
